analysis.summary: bench compare is a model sweeper wearing a setup-sweeper's name. cmd_compare (benchkit/cli.py:125-164) iterates one axis - the Hugging Face model id - rewriting MODEL_ID in start-qwen.sh via serving.swap_to (:137) and running runner.run (:147). The other two axes exist in the codebase but are not wired to it: serving.list_configs()/apply_config() (serving.py:56-77) already enumerate and install the six configs/ recipes, and hrunner.run (benchkit/harness/runner.py:10-39) already runs a suite through pi/opencode/claude-code, but compare calls neither. The reporting end is in better shape than the execution end - report.build() already ranks agentic runs by agent_score (report.py:139-140), already renders a per-run harness block (30, 88-92) and already prints sample-count noise caveats (239-245) - so most of the work is in cmd_compare and in result attribution, not in the report. The structural blocker is that runner.Config (runner.py:26-36) has no field naming the serving config or harness a run came from, so a ranked cross-setup table has nothing to key on.
analysis.details: Three dependencies shape the design. (1) Issue #55: compare cannot run agentic suites at all, and agentic is the only suite kind the harness axis supports (cmd_harness rejects non-agentic suites at cli.py:210-212). A harness sweep on top of a compare that KeyErrors on agentic suites is not buildable. (2) Issue #19, open: serving.swap_to/restart (serving.py:37-53) has no approval gate and cmd_compare calls it unconditionally; a config sweep multiplies unguarded restarts of a shared endpoint, which CLAUDE.md forbids outright. (3) Issue #37, open: cmd_compare's finally block (cli.py:153-156) calls serving.swap_to(original) unprotected, so a restore failure masks the original exception - and 'the original serving config is restored when the sweep ends, including on failure' is one of this issue's own acceptance criteria, which must not reintroduce that masking. Two design questions remain genuinely open. Restart cost: iteration must be grouped by serving config, restarting once per config rather than once per combination, or a six-config sweep becomes hours of engine init. Cross-harness comparability: the repo's own numbers (67.4 through the built-in loop vs 79.3 through opencode on identical weights) mean harness rows are not directly comparable, so the report must name the harness on every row and rank within a harness before declaring a global winner. Finally, configs/llamacpp-qwen3.8-27b-bench.sh is not a vLLM systemd recipe; serving.py's MODEL_RE/restart machinery cannot drive it, so the sweep must exclude or special-case it rather than blindly cross-producting.

options.name: Extend cmd_compare in place with --configs and --harnesses

files_to_modify.changes: Add --configs and --harnesses to the compare subparser; restructure cmd_compare's loop into config -> (model x harness x thinking), dispatching to runner.run or hrunner.run
Expose a config-swap helper with the #19 approval gate and non-vLLM recipe exclusion
Add serving_config/harness attribution fields to Config and carry them into the summary

options.test_strategy: Unit tests over the setup-enumeration and iteration-grouping helpers with serving stubbed
pros: Smallest diff; reuses report.build's existing ranking and noise machinery
One command, matching the epic's 'a single command produces a ranked report'
cons: cmd_compare's argparse surface and try/finally become dense

options.rejection_reason: Overloads an existing command whose current contract users rely on, and independent flags cross-product into invalid setups.

Add a guarded apply-and-restart path honoring the #19 approval guardrail; add a snapshot/restore of start-qwen.sh so the original config comes back on failure; skip non-vLLM recipes such as configs/llamacpp-qwen3.8-27b-bench.sh
Add serving_config and harness attribution to Config and propagate into summarize()'s output so each result JSON records the setup that produced it
Accept the same attribution so harness runs are labeled identically
Rank setups rather than models; print config + harness on every row; rank within a harness before naming a global winner; reuse the existing sample-count noise caveat (239-245)
Document which recipes are sweepable and why the llama.cpp one is not
Runbook entry for the sweep and its approval prompt

files_to_create.purpose: Unit tests: setup enumeration groups by config and restarts once per config; a declined approval performs no systemctl call and no launcher write; the original launcher is restored after an injected mid-sweep failure and the original exception is not masked; non-vLLM recipes are excluded; every emitted summary names its config and harness.

options.test_strategy: unittest in repo style with subprocess/systemctl and both run functions monkeypatched - no live endpoint, no restart, no writes under results/. Assert restart count equals the number of distinct configs, not the number of setups.
pros: Leaves bench compare's existing contract intact for anyone not opting in
A fresh implementation can get the restore-without-masking (#37) and approval-gate (#19) behavior right by construction
Fits the repo's existing per-subcommand cmd_* structure
cons: A second comparison command to maintain and document
Still needs #55's agentic dispatch and #19's guardrail before it can land honestly
options.risk_details: New command, so existing compare behavior cannot regress; the real risk stays concentrated in serving.py's restart path, which is exactly where the guardrail belongs

options.name: Declarative sweep spec file
options.summary: Accept --spec sweep.yaml enumerating setups, with per-setup sample overrides and explicit skips.
options.test_strategy: Spec parser tests plus the option-2 sweep tests
pros: Most flexible; natural home for per-setup sample counts
cons: Introduces a config-file format with no precedent in this repo - configs/ are .sh launchers, not declarative specs
Heaviest build for an issue already blocked twice
Would pull in a YAML dependency against a deliberately thin requirements.txt
options.risk_details: New file format and parser surface on top of an already-large feature
options.rejection_reason: Adds a new declarative file format with no precedent in a repo whose dependency floor is deliberately openai-only, for an issue that is already effort L and doubly blocked.

decision_record.root_cause: bench compare automates one axis of a three-axis question. cmd_compare (benchkit/cli.py:125-164) sweeps only the Hugging Face model id, rewriting MODEL_ID via serving.swap_to (:137) and always calling runner.run (:147). The config axis exists unused (serving.list_configs/apply_config, serving.py:56-77) and the harness axis exists unused (hrunner.run, benchkit/harness/runner.py:10-39). runner.Config (runner.py:26-36) records neither the serving config nor the harness, so nothing downstream can key a ranked cross-setup table.

selected_option.name: New bench sweep command over an explicit setup matrix
selected_option.summary: A bench sweep subcommand that runs explicit (config, harness, model, thinking) setups grouped by serving config - one guarded restart per config - and emits one ranked report naming the winning setup, with the original launcher restored on success and on failure.

decision_record.residual_risk: Two hard prerequisites outside this issue's own diff: #55 must land first or the harness axis has no working agentic path through compare, and #19's approval guardrail must exist or the sweep multiplies unguarded restarts of a shared endpoint in violation of CLAUDE.md. Cross-harness scores remain not directly comparable (67.4 vs 79.3 on identical weights per the repo's own README), so a single global winner is only meaningful within one harness; the report must say so. configs/llamacpp-qwen3.8-27b-bench.sh cannot be driven by serving.py's systemd/MODEL_RE machinery and must be excluded.
